2608.14370.title: A Hybrid LLM-Based Framework for Automated Security Annotation Generation in Business Process Models
2608.14370.paper_summary: The modelling and analysis of secure business processes require the incorporation of security annotations into process models. Although BPMN extensions, including SecBPMN2, exist for this purpose, the derivation of accurate and complete security annotations from natural-language specifications remains a manual, expert-intensive, and error-prone task. This paper presents a hybrid framework that takes a BPMN process model and a security requirements document as input and automatically generates security annotations adhering to the SecBPMN2 specification. The approach combines Large Language Model (LLM)--based semantic extraction with schema-constrained mapping, rule-based normalization, and deterministic validation. The framework is evaluated comprehensively on a curated dataset of 27 process models from various domains. The results indicate that it consistently produces structurally valid SecBPMN2 annotations with high schema completeness. Compared to human security analysts, the system achieves substantially higher precision (0.58 vs. 0.29) while maintaining comparable recall (0.52 vs. 0.50) and reduces erroneous or misplaced annotations by nearly 50%. In addition, annotation generation is significantly faster than manual annotation. These findings demonstrate that hybrid LLM- and rule-based automation can reduce modeling effort while improving consistency and reliability, thereby providing a scalable foundation for security-by-design BPM.
2608.14370.paper_summary_zh: 建模和分析安全業務流程需要將安全註釋納入流程模型中。儘管為此目的存在包括SecBPMN2在內的BPMN擴展，但從自然語言規範中推導出準確且完整的安全註釋仍然是一項手動、專家密集且容易出錯的任務。本文提出了一個混合框架，該框架將BPMN流程模型和安全需求文檔作為輸入，自動生成符合SecBPMN2規範的安全註釋。該方法結合了基於大型語言模型（LLM）的語義提取、模式約束映射、基於規則的標準化和確定性驗證。該框架在來自各個領域的27個流程模型的策展數據集上進行了全面評估。結果表明，它始終生成結構上有效的SecBPMN2註釋，並具有高模式完整性。與人類安全分析師相比，該系統在精確度上顯著提高（0.58對0.29），同時保持可比的召回率（0.52對0.50），並將錯誤或錯位的註釋減少近50%。此外，註釋生成的速度顯著快於手動註釋。這些發現表明，混合的LLM和基於規則的自動化可以減少建模工作，同時提高一致性和可靠性，從而為安全設計的BPM提供可擴展的基礎。
